stories.title: Two dead and evacuation under way as fires break out on Greek island
stories.summary: Two people have died and an evacuation is under way after two fires broke out within minutes of each other on a Greek island near Athens. Fire officials said nearly 200 firefighters were working to extinguish the flames on the island of Salamina and keep them from converging, Greek media report. The first blaze was reported at 14:40 local time (12:40 GMT) and spread rapidly due to high winds, according to officials on the island - which was under a high wildfire risk on Sunday. Some 90 people have so far been evacuated by sea, a coastguard spokesman told Greek broadcaster ERT. Five patrol boats have been sent to the area and several other private vessels are being made available for assistance, he added. A number of aircraft and 50 fire engines have been deployed to the blaze. Salamina Deputy Mayor Thodoris Zannis said firefighters were trying to keep the fires from burning over a mountain on the island and forming one major wildfire. Salamina sits just west of Athens and has some 37,000 residents, many of them elderly. Firefighters across Europe have been facing a series of wildfires this weekend, fuelled by high heat.

stories.title: Italy: Four Renaissance artworks stolen from Messina museum in Sicily
stories.summary: Four artworks by Renaissance painter Antonello da Messina have been stolen from the Museo Regionale in Messina, Sicily, overnight on August 15. The thieves took three panels from his Polittico di San Gregorio, depriving the city of part of the only surviving works by the painter still held in his hometown. Italian authorities have launched an investigation. FRANCE 24's Seema Gupta, correspondent in Italy, has the latest.

stories.title: Kushner expected to visit Israel next week - source
stories.summary: A source in the Israeli government told TASS
article_sentences: US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner is expected to visit Israel in the coming days, an Israeli government source told TASS.
"As for Kushner, the answer is ‘yes,’" he said when asked whether Israel expects him next week.

stories.title: Senegal: Saint-Louis’ centuries-old pirogue racing tradition
stories.summary: In Saint-Louis, Senegal, traditional pirogue races are keeping alive a centuries-old tradition dating back nearly 200 years. Held in the fishing district of Guet Ndar, the 3.5-kilometre race brings together dozens of rowers and huge crowds, turning the event into both a major sporting competition and a celebration of local culture. But despite the race's popularity and the money it generates, competitors are not paid and are calling for greater recognition for the sport.

stories.summary: Hong Kong customs has said it is actively following up on a case involving a London‑based beauty chain after a woman complained that she cheated into paying more than HK$60,000 (US$7,700) for products and raised concerns about the company’s operations.
